item.description: ui : Discover & Download Models from HF Hub (#29584) * common : resolve - download tags and list cached sidecars A Q4_0-mtp style tag now resolves the sidecar file when no model file matches it, so a solo draft or mmproj download actually pulls the file. Assisted-by: pi:GLM-5.3-Flash * ui : add the discover models components The Discover surface: the curated-catalog list with its search and skeletons, the details pane with its readme, metadata, Hub stats and download options, and the standalone download progress bar that replaces the plain one. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : put the discover view in the models manager The manager dialog gains its second view: the Discover Models call to action fades the table out, slides the title with its compass mark, and fades the discover surface in; the arrow button returns to the table. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash # Conflicts: # tools/ui/src/lib/components/ui/button/button.svelte * ui : add the Enable Discover Models setting The flag gates browsing and downloading HuggingFace GGUF models, so it is declared on the discover layer; the repo-tree lookup in the manager layer above reads it from here. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : resume model downloads from the pause point A stopped download keeps its partial file instead of deleting it, so re-posting the tag resumes from disk. The first progress record now carries the resume offset, the paused snapshot survives into the resumed entry, and a pause settles as soon as it is requested. Assisted-by: pi * ui : lead the discover list with downloads The discover sidebar lists running downloads above the suggested models, and steps aside while a query is active. A paused download stays in the manager table, where it is resumed or dropped. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make resuming a paused download work Re-posting the tag of a paused download hit the router's "already exists" check, because a paused download parks its entry as DOWNLOADED until the next reload: a download entry that is not running is now replaced and resumed. The UI keeps the paused row when the request still fails, instead of dropping it and looking finished. Assisted-by: pi * ui : remember unfinished model downloads A partial file is named after its content hash, so nothing on disk says which model it belongs to once the router restarts. The router now keeps the tags of the downloads it started, clears a tag when the download finishes or is deleted, and lists what is left as still downloading without starting anything. The UI adopts those tags as paused on every list fetch, so a refresh or a fresh open shows an incomplete download and can resume it from the files already on disk. Assisted-by: pi * ui : show a paused download's state on its chip A paused quant chip reads as paused at rest, the way a running one shows its spinner, and offers the resume action on hover. Assisted-by: pi * ui : collapse the download options by default The copyable download command starts collapsed so the option rows lead; expanding it stays one click away. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep decision models out of the hub lists Decision models answer with calibrated probabilities instead of text, so llama-ui cannot run them: the hub data layer drops them from the catalog and every search, keyed by the decision-model tag or a text-classification pipeline. Assisted-by: pi * ui : read download tags as quant and sidecar A : - tag now parses into its quant and sidecar instead of one opaque quant token, and ModelsService.draftSidecarsByRepo collects the router listing's sidecar-only entries per repo, replacing the inline copy in the models store. Assisted-by: pi * ui : act on tracked downloads from the table rows The table passes its clusters' draft sub-lines to the model rows. Assisted-by: pi * ui : give downloads a configuration pane of their own Selecting a tracked download opens the pane in a download mode: live progress with pause, resume and cancel, and See in Discover, instead of metadata and load actions that a model without files cannot offer. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep discover off by default and couple it with the hub setting Discover Models starts unchecked. Assisted-by: pi * common: settle sidecar names on the listing and drop unfinished partials An infix or trailing sidecar token is ambiguous: draft heads use it (Model-MTP-BF16.gguf), so do full models with embedded heads (Model-Q8D-MTP.gguf). A quant tag always carries its bit count, so a sidecar named after no quant (mtp-Model-it.gguf) gets the bare tag: the listing, the plan and remove all use it. An imatrix tag resolves into a plan slot of its own, downloaded but never wired into the params. remove resolves the tag the way a download does and deletes the partial files of every planned blob, so cancelling a running download or dropping one left unfinished by an earlier run leaves nothing on disk. Assisted-by: pi * ui : trim the download option comments and highlight the chat template The comment verbosity the options panel and its chips carried shrinks to the non-obvious why, and the chat template dialog renders through SyntaxHighlightedCode as jinja instead of a plain pre block. Assisted-by: pi * common: only a .gguf file is a sidecar, and mmproj/imatrix as whole words A non-GGUF file named like a sidecar (quantization-mmproj-Q8_0.json) is picked as the mmproj, and a sidecar word inside a longer word of a model name (Phi-2-OmniMatrix.i1-Q4_K_M.gguf) drops the model. * ui: dedupe draft sidecar badges per quant The draft sidecar badges deduped by kind and repo without the quant, so with a draft cached at two quants only one badge survived, and a delete of the other main quant found no badge to remove its sidecar with. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * nit: Remove + before draft sidecar badge * server: list unfinished downloads as incomplete A download that never finished was reported as "downloading", the same status a live download carries, so a client could not tell a running download from a dead one. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * server: download a model with its sidecars as -hf does Resolution goes back to master. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : post the model's sidecar kinds with its download The store keeps one download per model: the chip's kinds ride along with the model's own sidecars, and a download row no longer expands into one row per sidecar. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : name why a download is refused A model that is already downloading, or that is running, answered "already exists". It now says which: "is already downloading", or "is running, unload it first", both before the resumable check. The router test covers the two. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : post a download once per click Two quick clicks on the same chip posted twice, and the second answer was "already exists". Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep a plain download row the height of the others The sub-lines wrapper of a download row was rendered even with nothing in it, so its padding made the row taller than a plain one and the overlaid progress bar sat in that empty strip. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : ignore a pause while the download POST is still on its way The chip reads as downloading before the server answers, so a quick second click unloaded a model that had not started and left the store neither in flight nor paused. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : offer a missing draft as its own chip A model already on disk without its draft had no way to add it: the quant chip carried the draft, so it read as a download of both. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : list a paused sidecar download by the files on disk A model on disk whose sidecar download stops keeps its unfinished record, and the listing reported the kinds that record plans as if they were on disk: the UI checked a draft that never landed and offered no way to add it. The planned kinds now stand in only while the download runs. * chore: Clean up comments * server : list sidecars only for a model that resolves from a HF repo A preset on a local file has no HF repo, yet the listing resolved its name as one: the plan threw on the invalid repo format and GET /models failed for every model. The sidecars now come from the repo a preset names or a cached model is listed under, and a local file lists without them. * common : fix download cancel regression Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common : preserve model partials when removing sidecars Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * server : one sidecar table and an unfinished downloads class Address review from @ggerganov. The sidecar kinds live in one table in common/download, mapping each name to its download option and plan file; the server validates, builds its options and lists cached sidecars through it instead of its own lists. The unfinished downloads move into server_unfinished_downloads, a record with its own mutex and a struct per entry, and server_models exposes them through unfinished_downloads_get and unfinished_downloads_remove. * common: one sidecar table, and removals that keep shared files The resolution, the cached listing and the removal follow a single table of sidecar kinds, so a kind is declared once with its file keyword, whether it is a draft, its option and its plan file. The server reads the same table for the kinds it accepts, the default sidecars and the child flags. Removing a tag keeps the files another cached tag still loads, such as an mmproj named after the removed quant. A sidecar removed on its own goes for every tag that resolves it. An unfinished download records the exact paths of its partials when it starts. A removal deletes those without asking the hub, and keeps a partial another recorded download also writes. The record is taken once the child is spawned, and the files go under the models lock, so a download of the same tag cannot start while they are removed. * server: drop stale partials and refuse a tag that resolves nothing Recording a download again deletes the partials of the earlier record that the new plan no longer writes, such as those of an older hub revision or of a sidecar the new request leaves out. A posted tag that resolves no file of the repo is refused before the download starts. Removing a model follows a single path, whether the reload erased its entry during the wait or not. * server: fix the CI race between the router download tests The pytest workers run in parallel on one shared cache, so a download test could find the file another test had just fetched and see no progress, or start from the unfinished downloads record another test wrote. Each download test now runs on an empty cache of its own. * server: refuse a DELETE of an unknown name and decide downloads in load() A DELETE of a name that is neither a model nor a recorded download went to common_download_remove, and without a tag it wiped the whole repo cache, including the files of a loaded quant or of a download on its way. Such a name is now not found, as it was before. A POST that downloads over an existing entry checked its state outside the lock, so a load of the same model in between got its instance killed. The checks now run in load(), under the lock, right before the spawn. The fake load time of the tests applies to model loads only, since a download worker loads none. * server: add incomplete_sidecars to the /models API A sidecar added to a cached model and then paused kept its record, but the listing showed only the complete model, so a fresh UI lost the pause. The model entry now carries incomplete_sidecars, the kinds its unfinished download has not written yet; a POST with the kind resumes one and a DELETE with it drops its partial. * common : drop a kept partial when a resume gets 416 Now that partials survive between attempts, an old or complete partial makes every retry fail with the same 416. Delete it so the next attempt can start over from zero. Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common: drop a kept partial when a resume gets 200 A server that ignores the range answers 200 to a resume, and the kept partial then fails every attempt the same way a 416 does. Drop it as well, so the next attempt starts over without a range. * server: refuse a download that shares a partial with one on its way Two downloads of quants that share a file, the mmproj or an mtp picked by the closest bits, appended to the same partial and renamed a file with interleaved bytes. item.description: tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test ran on were not a Muse Spark. Per-tensor rules lived inside the write path, where a flag picked the values of a tensor inside each of the two branches that store them, so a new rule meant a new flag threaded through both. The file asks to be rid of that in a TODO of its own. Give each rule a filler, pick one from a table keyed on a substring of the tensor name, and keep a single write path behind it. Mamba moves into the table and Muse Spark joins it: the gate filler draws the raw weight once per block and resolves alpha and beta the way the conversion does. Over a thousand seeds on a CPU build the worst case drops from 1.36e-05 to 2.48e-06 and the median from 4.10e-06 to 5.48e-07, with no seed above the threshold. The other 131 models come out identical to the bit, since no other architecture carries these tensors. ctest is green on a CPU build and on a CUDA build. * tests: draw every tensor filler from fill_normal The fillers repeated the generator and the distribution each time. The normal draw now takes its key and the other fillers transform its values, so the generator lives in one place. item.description: model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support (#30673) * model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support Kolibri-1 is a bilingual German/English MoE reasoning model with 78B parameters and 3.46B active per token: 50 layers, 384 routed experts plus one shared expert. Attention interleaves four sliding layers at a 513 window with one full layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE. GQA runs 48 query heads against 4 KV heads at head_dim 128 with a QK-RMSNorm, and every block carries four RMSNorms, so the attention and the MLP output are normalized before they rejoin the residual stream. Routing picks the experts from logits + expert_bias and weights them with the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code, it goes through the generic weight_scale_inv path. Three tensor names are added to the mapping (post_attn_norm, post_ffn_norm, moe.router.expert_bias) and the 128k vocabulary registers the qwen2 pre-tokenizer by hash. The arch is registered in test-llama-archs, with GQA and the sliding window pattern. item.description: common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client (#21752) * common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client common_http_client() was ignoring standard proxy env vars, causing downloads via -hf and similar flags to fail silently in environments behind an HTTP proxy (corporate networks, air-gapped infra, etc.). Checks HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy for https:// URLs and HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy for http:// URLs, in that order. If a proxy URL is set and parseable, passes it to httplib's set_proxy() and set_proxy_basic_auth() as appropriate. Malformed proxy URLs are silently ignored so existing callers aren't affected. Fixes #21694 * common: drop misleading comment about generic proxy fallback The comment referenced a 'generic one' that doesn't exist in the code — both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are scheme-specific. Reviewer noted the mismatch. Addresses review feedback from @ServeurpersoCom. * common : warn when the proxy URL from the environment is malformed * common : honor NO_PROXY when selecting the http proxy * ci : retrigger checks (test-thread-safety flake) * common : bypass the proxy for loopback destinations llama cli talks to its spawned server on 127.0.0.1 through common_http_client, so with HTTP_PROXY set and no NO_PROXY the health polling went to the corporate proxy, which rejects loopback targets, and the wait loop never exits ("Loading model..." hangs forever). A remote proxy can never reach the client machine's own loopback, so these destinations are now always contacted directly, before NO_PROXY is consulted: localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and 0.0.0.0. Similar to Go's net/http. Proxy handling for downloads and remote --server-base endpoints is unchanged. item.description: model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) (#30616) * model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) Muse Spark Open is a latent space MoE: the residual stream stays at 8192 while the 256 experts live in 4096, with a projection down and up around them, top-8 sigmoid routing with a correction bias. Attention interleaves three sliding layers at a 2048 window with rope for one global layer without rope, with a sigmoid output gate and a weightless QK-norm. Residuals are norm preserving, their gate is folded at conversion time. Vision reuses the Muse Glimmer tower. Audio is a causal convolutional pyramid with no attention and no spectrogram, four stages folding 16, 6, 5 and 4 samples into the channel dim, one embedding per 80 ms of 24 kHz. The quantizer keeps the latent projections and the attention gate at Q8_0, a little over 1% of the weights, since the whole residual stream passes through them and the low-bit types turned the output into a repeating loop. The model saver writes the post norm epsilon, and the arch is registered in test-llama-archs. item.description: ## Overview llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (--moe-cache-mib, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (common_chat_session, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0. ### Highlights - New GPU cache for host-memory MoE experts (--moe-cache-mib): experts run on the GPU from an LRU cache, up to 2.2x faster decode #29887 - The expert cache is now shared across multiple GPUs #30112 - LiliCorr speculative decoding: candidate selection with a small draft transformer on top of DFlash #30506 - GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path #29928 - K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat template, -sm tensor splitting #29535 - Prism Bonsai 2 27B ternary model support #29600 - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embedding model #30054 - New decision models: LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-omni-600M, vLLM decision 2, vLLM d3 and pplx-decider #30110 #30114 #30378 #30383 #30044 - PLaMo-3 tokenizer implements reference pre-segmentation for exact tokenization parity #30045 - RPC server supports -sm tensor (tensor-parallel RPC, RPC protocol v8) #26610 - Server now listens on port 9931 by default instead of 8080 #30159 ### API changes - include/llama.h: new moe_cache_size context param for the host-expert GPU cache #29887 - include/llama.h: new LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_PLAMO3 vocab type #30045 - include/llama.h: llama_perf_context_data reports graph reallocations during inference #30329 - include/llama.h: embeddings now skips the LM head when a pooling type other than NONE is used #30445 - include/llama.h: llama_batch_ext_set_embd_state returns false when the context has no state embedding, M-RoPE order documented #30506 - tools/server: chat layer refactored around common_chat_session with feed() / finish() #30210 - tools/server: formatted chat output is now an array of parts instead of a single string #30389 - tools/server: default listening port changed to 9931 (Docker images keep 8080 inside the container) #30159 ### New models - K2 Horizon: dense and MoVA variants with conversion, tokenizer, chat template and -sm tensor support #29535 - Prism Bonsai 2 27B (ternary) #29600 - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embeddings #30054 - LiquidAI d1-3B and d1-omni-600M decision models #30110 #30114 - vLLM decision 2 and vLLM d3 models #30378 #30383 - pplx-decider decision model #30044 - MiniCPM-V 4.7 multimodal model #29416 - Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B #30520 - maion-coder architecture #29778 - Mellum: MoE gating parameters read from GGUF and unified RoPE handling #30578 - LiliCorr draft model conversion and graph #30506 - Rerankers: classifier_activation support, exact GELU for ModernBERT encoders #29692 #30108 ### Core changes - Speculative decoding: MTP for GLM5-Next, LiliCorr drafts, correct mtmd handling in MTP graphs #29928 #30506 #30257 - Speculative decoding: shared nextn tensor flags with consolidated row cropping and sched re-reserve on flag change #30097 #30017 #30020 - Speculative decoding: fixed draft sampling and rejection handling, DFlash output head sharing #30095 #30111 - New --spec-draft-n-ubatch to size the draft context batch separately and save VRAM #30459 - MoE expert cache: host-memory experts served from a device LRU cache, supported over multiple GPUs #29887 #30112 - Embedding models: skip the logits buffer and the LM head when pooling is enabled (up to 10x less VRAM) #30255 #30445 - Embedding graphs: reordered get_rows, dropped the redundant t_embd expand and leftover ggml_cont calls #30160 #30461 #30198 - No-cache attention: padded KV dimension and KQ bias, avoided graph reallocations #30416 #30446 #30439 - k-pool models: selection built in the causal mask layout, fixed a scatter data race on shared sequences #30480 #29994 - GLM5-Next sparse attention: removed the gather path #30042 - KV cache: honor LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_PARTIAL_ONLY so draft checkpoints stop carrying the full KV #30514 - Prefetching: merge ranges before issuing system prefetch calls, never map foreign ranges into a backend buffer #30532 #30405 - Sampling: greedy selection for eligible temperature-zero chains, backend sampling graph kept static across ubatches #29797 #30223 - Tokenizers: PLaMo-3 pre-segmentation and FiM tokens, opt-in NFC normalization for Unigram, strict UTF-8 validation #30045 #30090 #30390 #30485 - Jinja: fixed loop variable scoping, Python-compatible tojson rendering, faster context copy #30533 #30483 #30362 #30562 - Model split: distribute layers evenly when no device reports free memory #29677 ### Multi-modality changes - Added mtmd_build_inp_attn_mask for building non-causal multimodal attention masks #30259 - Added cohere2 vision encoder support #30062 - MTP drafts now handle mtmd inputs, Qwen3.8 Flash Next accepts image embeddings #30257 #30397 - New multimodal architectures: MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, EmbeddingGemma-2 (vision + audio) #29416 #30520 #30054 ### Server changes - /v1/systemone extended to the new decision models: d1-3B, d1-omni, vLLM decision 2/d3, pplx-decider #30110 #30114 #30378 #30383 #30044 - Chat refactor: session-based parsing and part-based formatted output #30210 #30389 - Generated text and tokens are now accumulated as parser input, preparing token-aware parsing #29876 - Prompt cache: only restorable slot states are saved, so rerank and embedding requests no longer fill the cache #30498 - Prompt cache: child tasks prefer empty slots and preserve the state they would overwrite #30567 - A pinned busy slot is left untouched until the request can run on it #30295 - Slot save/restore now keeps context checkpoints and the draft model state #26004 #30574 - Fixed an off-by-two in the SWA reuse threshold that discarded restored states #30580 - Fixed a stack-overflow crash when escaping special tokens with std::regex #30243 - LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH environment variable for --slot-save-path #30272 - New per-component server tests; vendored cpp-httplib updated to 0.61.0 #30312 #30494 #30134 #30081 ### UI changes - New Models Manager: one table of all served models with expandable quants, search, filters, sorting and favorites #29583 - Row actions: load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, resumable downloads with progress #29583 - Model configuration side drawer with model info, chat template and "start a new chat" / "use in this chat" actions #29583 - Models manager follow-ups: GGUF training context, favorite UX, filter and sort fixes #30228 - Fixed ui_settings not being applied on the first visit in router mode #29668 - Fixed text attachment preview overflow for large pasted text #29898 - Fixed the default agentic turns limit falling back to 10 instead of 100 #30582 ### ggml changes - ggml updated to v0.27.0: the backend scheduler gains user callbacks for split weight copying and compute-buffer reallocation, and the RPC protocol is bumped to v8 for tensor-parallel RPC servers. Backends gained chunked gated-delta-net kernels on CUDA/HIP, KleidiAI SME2 k-quant matmuls and AVX2 Q2_0 dot products on CPU, L2-aware coopmat2 scheduling and bf16 activations on Vulkan, reordered-layout MoE kernels (MXFP4, IQ3, Q5_K, grouped XMX GEMM) on SYCL, dp4a MoE GEMMs on OpenCL, tensor-API and wider-head-dim flash attention on Metal, and a DMA/HVX copy overhaul with pooling and 3D im2col ops on Hexagon. Correctness work focused on non-contiguous and strided views, grid and workgroup size limits, out-of-bounds accesses and well-defined mul_mat_id behavior for duplicate expert ids; symbol visibility item.description: server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts, while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank, embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt cache Embedding and rerank tasks never reuse their state, so their slots are cleared on release like child slots and the cache only holds states that a later task can restore. Infill and decision tasks now restore from the cache too, which replaces the cache_pending flag. Decision models disable the prompt cache unless --cache-ram is given, since their states seldom repeat. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107) * sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing sees the same benefit. Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently producing a degraded backend. item.description: ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N]. The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires: no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way, since swapping two dimensions when one of them is 1 changes nothing. The batched path matters to downstream audio projects where several synthesis lanes share a single graph. Nothing in mtmd batches a vocoder today, each one streams one flow and carries its left context between calls, but the op is correct now if one of them grows a lane dimension. * ggml: build the same conv_1d graph for every batch size Address review from ggerganov: drop the N == 1 branch of ggml_conv_1d. The GEMM result is always reshaped to [OC, N, OL] and permuted back, as ggml_conv_2d does, so every batch size builds the same graph. For N == 1 this adds a cont on an already ordered tensor. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings (#30445) * graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings A context that extracts pooled embeddings outputs one vector per sequence, but every model still expanded its LM head, so the graph computed n_vocab logits per token and the context kept a host buffer for them. The models now only declare t_logits, and set_outputs() expands it unless the context extracts embeddings with a pooling type other than NONE. Since the toggle changes the graph shape for a pooled context, set_embeddings() schedules a re-reserve in that case. * graph: drop the redundant t_embd expand Address review from @CISC: with embeddings on, build_pooling() already expands its output for every pooling type, and a decoder graph without embeddings does not read t_embd, so set_outputs() only expands t_logits. * graph: add build_logits() for the LM head output Address review from @ggerganov: the LM head is expanded by a dedicated build_logits(), called from llama_model::build_graph() like build_pooling(), and set_outputs() only marks the outputs again. * graph: call build_logits() before build_sampling() Address review from @ggerganov: build_sampling() reads t_logits, so the LM head is built first. item.description: tests : consolidate context state tests into test-llama-context (#30023) * tests : consolidate the context state tests into test-llama-context test-save-load-state, test-recurrent-state-rollback and test-state-restore-fragmented check the same object from three places: the KV cache and the recurrent state of a llama_context, saved, loaded, copied, rolled back. Each had its own main, its own loop over the models, its own copy of the token and the comparison helpers, and a run of all three loaded the same models several times. They are one binary now, and the case is the unit of the test: tests/llama-context/test-case.h the interface a case implements tests/llama-context/cases-kv.cpp the cases of the KV cache tests/llama-context/cases-rs.cpp the cases of the recurrent state tests/llama-context/test-util.cpp tokens, generation, comparison tests/llama-context/test-runner.cpp the models of a case, on threads tests/llama-context/test-log.cpp the log file of a model A run is a table: a row per model, a column per case, a cell holds the verdict of that pair. The models load on several threads (-j, --threads, min(cores, 4) by default), the table is printed when it is complete and the log of a model that failed is printed after it, in the order of the rows. A case returns a verdict and the reason for it, and the runner is the only one who reports - the test does not use tests/testing.h, a run over 130 models is a matrix of verdicts and not a tree of subtests. Staging no longer travels through the environment: llama_model_set_attn_rot replaces the LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE variable, which a model loaded in one thread used to change for the models the other threads were loading, and llama_memory_get_buffers is added for the cases that copy the buffers of a memory. common_log_set_stdo keeps the console quiet while the table is being built. ggml_aligned_malloc allocates with posix_memalign when the thread sanitizer is on. On macOS it allocates with the Mach VM, which the sanitizer does not intercept, so it never sees a page range change hands and reports the first write into recycled memory as a race - 30 of them in this test, and every one of them false. item.description: metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids (#30373) * metal : fix mul_mat_id limits and kernel name * metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 assumed at most one match per token and a fixed capacity of ne21 entries per expert, which produced wrong or dropped output rows and could overflow into the slice of the next expert when the ids contain duplicates. build a compact per-expert list of the (token, slot) entries instead: - pass 1 counts the entries of every expert, thread 0 computes the offsets of the expert slices (tpe now holds [base, count]) - pass 2 writes the entries with one unconditional store per token (conditional stores of divergent lanes are very slow), the dummy value of the tokens without a match lands on a padding slot of the slice that is never read - duplicates are handled by a rare branch - kernel_mul_mm_id reads the base/count of its expert and loops over the entry tiles that do not fit into the grid The ids buffer is sized as ne20*ne21 + ne02 (entries + padding). 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, llama-bench is within run-to-run variance of the previous behavior. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * metal : make mul_mat_id map0 ne02 a function constant use FOR_UNROLL for the id loops of kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 and turn ne02 into the function constant FC_mul_mm_id_map0_ne02 (FC_MUL_MM + 7), so that the threadgroup offsets of cnt/bas/sids and the prefix-sum bound fold at compile time. the pipeline name now encodes ne02 (same convention as the ssm_conv nc/silu constants) and the map0 pipeline is compiled with the constant value set. ne02 is no longer part of ggml_metal_kargs_mul_mm_id_map0 - the dispatch grid still comes from the tensor ne[2] on the host. no measurable perf change: 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, op-level and llama-bench results are within run variance. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * cont : clean-up + TODO * metal : dispatch mul_mat_id entry tiles from the prepass follow the approach of the vulkan implementation (#29998): instead of launching a grid over experts x ne21 entry tiles and letting most of the threadgroups early exit, kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 now also emits a row map - the total tile count plus one (expert, first entry, valid rows) descriptor per 32-entry tile that has work. kernel_mul_mm_id is launched with a static upper bound on the number of tiles (full tiles over all entries plus at most one partial tile per expert), reads its descriptor and processes a single tile - the tail early exits. This removes the round loop that was needed to cover duplicate ids past the grid (register pressure: th_max 768 -> back to the plain mul_mm level) and duplicates are now handled implicitly, since they only produce more descriptors within the bound. The grid shrinks by ~8-16x on typical shapes (e.g. 128 experts, 8 used, 512 tokens: 128 tiles instead of 2048 entry tiles, of which 94% only launched to exit) and ne21 is no longer needed by the mm kernel kargs. 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass. llama-bench (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0) is now faster than master on all pp sizes (pp2048/4096/8192 +2%, pp512 +0.5%), tg32 unchanged. item.description: llama : report compute graph reallocations during inference (#30329) Add an optional ggml_backend_sched_realloc_callback that user code registers with ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback to be notified when the buffers reserved for a graph are not sufficient and have to be reserved again. The callback reports whether the backend assignments and the graph size changed since the previous scheduling. llama_context registers the callback when creating the scheduler (wrapped into the new llama_context::sched_new helper) and treats the reallocations that follow a change of the backend assignments as expected, counting the rest by graph size - unchanged or changed from the previously scheduled graph. Both counters are reported on one line in the perf stats.
